deep.reconstruction:
Setting (cote 154, 'systèmes de pseudo-droites', Jan. 1984). D is a relative position (combinatorial type) of n pseudo-lines, drawn as on the previous page: a disc whose boundary carries the 2n ends of the n pseudo-lines. Pol(D) is the associated boundary 2n-gon, so Aut Pol(D) ≅ D_{2n} is the dihedral group of order 4n (Grothendieck indexes it by the number of vertices). Grothendieck considers a 'surface' 𝒳, presumably a 2-dimensional cell complex, whose points are non-super-singular relative positions. Its paths are of three kinds: (i) ordinary specializations/generalizations of weight ±1, i.e. triangle flips or Ringel mutations; (ii) crossings of super-singular positions through an edge; (iii) crossings through a vertex where at least 3 pseudo-lines meet ('weight ≥3'). Over 𝒳 there is a principal D_{2n}-covering, given by the identifications of Pol(D) along paths, with monodromy π_1(𝒳,D) → Aut Pol(D) ≅ D_{2n}.

Claim 1 (checked, he says). This monodromy is surjective. For every edge or vertex of Pol(D), the loop 'half-turn of D around that edge or vertex' has monodromy equal to the reflection of the 2n-gon through it. Reflections through edges together with reflections through vertices generate D_{2n}.

Claim 2. Now forbid crossings of super-singular positions, giving a smaller space 𝒳̃ (the exact wording is illegible). The same argument only yields the reflections through edges. In a 2n-gon these generate an index-2 subgroup ≅ D_n: the even rotations plus the edge reflections. He notes, correctly, that D_{2n} has exactly three index-2 subgroups: the rotation group C_{2n}, the subgroup generated by edge reflections, and the subgroup generated by vertex reflections. So the image of π_1(𝒳̃) has index 1 or 2.

Claim 3. Making a half-turn around a super-singular position, or crossing it, acts by a rotation of 'amplitude n+1' (circled). He then studies the effect on Σ_a(D), the set of circumscribed polygons, and on two other two-element sets Σ_s(D) and ω(D), which serve as invariants detecting the index-2 quotient.

The next page completes the argument. For n odd the parity of n+1 forces surjectivity. For n even, he compares a loop l with ν super-singular crossings to the loop l' in which each crossing is replaced by a half-turn: they act oppositely on Σ_a. Starting from a D_0 with a suitable vertex s_0 of even order, he gets a loop in 𝒳̃ acting nontrivially on Σ(D_0). Conclusion: π_1(𝒳̃) → D_{2n} is surjective in all cases, i.e. the principal D_{2n}-covering is connected.

Purpose: connectedness and monodromy of the natural dihedral 'labelling' covering over the combinatorial moduli space of pseudo-line arrangements. This fits his programme of treating spaces of relative positions as geometric or topological objects (cf. the Esquisse's interest in 'tame' combinatorial moduli spaces).
errors: The algebra is correct as far as legible. The edge reflections of a 2n-gon generate a dihedral subgroup of order 2n (index 2), and D_{2n} has exactly three index-2 subgroups, as he says.
'D_n^+ (d'indice n?)' must mean the rotation subgroup of index 2 in the rotation group C_{2n}, i.e. the even rotations; 'indice n' would be wrong.
The rotation 'amplitude n+1' and the effect on Σ_a(D) are asserted, not proved, on this page.
The parity argument for n even depends on a vertex s_0 'd'ordre pair' existing in a chosen D_0; it is only sketched on the next page.

The interplay between the two notions (𝒳 with super-singular crossings vs 𝒳̃ without) and the precise definition of 𝒳̃ are not fully legible, so the logical status of the final claim (surjectivity for 𝒳̃) cannot be fully verified here.

ideas.what: Space/complex 𝒳 of combinatorial types (relative positions) of n pseudo-lines, with edges given by weight ±1 specializations/generalizations (triangle flips) and crossings of super-singular (multiple-point) positions
ideas.modern_name: Mutation/flip graph and its 2-complex for simple pseudoline arrangements (rank-3 uniform oriented matroids); stratification by degenerations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956, connectivity under mutations); Goodman–Pollack (1980s); Manin–Schechtman / Ziegler (higher Bruhat orders); Björner–Las Vergnas–Sturmfels–White–Ziegler (Oriented Matroids, 1993)
ideas.where_published: Pseudo-line notes are only alluded to around Esquisse d'un programme / Récoltes et Semailles; not developed in print (unsure about details)

ideas.what: Monodromy representation π_1(𝒳,D) → Aut Pol(D) ≅ D_{2n}, with half-turn loops realizing reflections through edges and vertices of the boundary 2n-gon
ideas.modern_name: Monodromy of the principal dihedral covering of labelled arrangements over unlabelled ones; connectedness of the labelled realization/flip space
ideas.usually_credited_to: No standard attribution known; related to fundamental groups of flip complexes and to Deligne/Salvetti-type complexes for reflection arrangements

ideas.what: Classification of index-2 subgroups of the dihedral group of a 2n-gon (rotations, edge-reflection subgroup, vertex-reflection subgroup)
Using parity invariants (the action on two-element sets Σ_a, Σ_s, ω of circumscribed polygons) to detect the index-2 quotient, and comparing super-singular crossings with half-turns
ideas.modern_name: Sign/orientation-type invariant of the monodromy; local monodromy around codimension-2 degeneration strata

missed.claim: A (sketched) computation that the natural dihedral D_{2n}-covering over the space of combinatorial types of n pseudo-lines is connected. The space has 2-cells around degenerate positions, both with and without crossing super-singular positions. Surjectivity is obtained via half-turn loops plus a parity argument depending on n mod 2.
missed.quote: π_1(X̃, D) → Aut Pol(D) ≃ D_2n soit surjectif ... L'image de π_1(X̃) dans D_2n est donc d'indice 1 ou 2.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Fundamental groups and monodromy of flip/mutation complexes of pseudoline arrangements (and higher Bruhat orders) are studied, but the dihedral relabelling monodromy and its parity subtleties do not appear to be standard results. This is a small but concrete unpublished computation.

missed.claim: Grothendieck treats the combinatorial moduli of pseudoline arrangements as a topological space (a 'surface' with loops around degeneration loci) carrying a principal covering. This is akin to treating it as a combinatorial analogue of the moduli spaces M_{0,n} with their dihedral symmetries, in the spirit of the Esquisse.
missed.quote: le revêtement X̃, de groupe D_2n est connexe (next page)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It links oriented-matroid flip complexes with the Esquisse's programme on fundamental groups of moduli spaces and their 'tame' cell decompositions. The literature (MacPherson's combinatorial Grassmannians, Mnëv) developed this largely independently.

deep.surprise_reason: A genuine, partially finished monodromy/connectedness computation on a space of pseudoline arrangements, apparently unpublished. However, it is modest in scope, the group theory is elementary, and the ambient ideas (flip connectivity, oriented matroids) are well developed elsewhere.

'copulatoire[?] de poids ≥ 3' is plausible as a reading.
'D_n^+ (d'indice n[?] ...)' likely '(d'indice 2 ...)' referring to the even rotations.
'est des effets [?] sur' likely 'a pour effet sur' / 'a des effets sur'.
'pour voir si l'A lacet en D_0' should read 'pour voir si un lacet en D_0'.
The date '5.1.84' is plausible (could be read 5.I.84).
The line defining X̃ ('le domaine X de b.g. des lieux superscritiques') probably means the complement in 𝒳 of the super-singular loci; 'superscritiques' should be 'supersinguliers'.
